generator_metadata.summary: A 0-background grid ordinarily contains 2-6 distinct-colored singleton seeds from {2,3,4,6,7,9}; the strict n_seeds override also supports the one-seed boundary. Seeds are at pairwise Manhattan distance at least 3, so their radius-one orthogonal halos do not overlap or erase another seed. Preserve the seeds and paint every in-bounds orthogonal background neighbor cyan (8). Position profiles exercise interior, edge, corner, and mixed clipping cases.

previous_catalog_record.summary: 0-bg grid (h, w~7-10) with 2-4 ISOLATED SINGLETON SEED cells in DISTINCT colors from {2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 9}. Seeds placed at Manhattan distance ≥ 3 between any pair so their halos don't overlap or erase other seeds. Rule (EXPAND SEEDS TO RADIUS-1 ORTHOGONAL HALO IN COLOR-8): For EACH SEED at (r, c) with color C: PAINT the 4 CARDINAL NEIGHBORS — (r-1, c), (r+1, c), (r, c-1), (r, c+1) — with COLOR-8 (cyan), clipping at grid edges. The seed cell stays color C. Net: each colored seed sprouts a cyan + halo around it.

scope: Accepted generator repair; finite reviewer evidence, no new maintainer execution

sequential_dependency.intermediate: An integer coverage grid aligned with the input; each background cell carries a value from 0 through 4 rather than a binary covered flag.
sequential_dependency.step_a: For every original background cell, count how many nonzero source seeds are exactly one orthogonal step away.
sequential_dependency.step_b: Preserve every source seed, leave count-zero cells at 0, paint count-one cells cyan (8), and in overlap_highlight paint count-two-or-more cells blue (1).
sequential_dependency.why_b_depends_on_a: Step B must distinguish count 1 from counts 2 through 4. Clipping Step A to a boolean covered/not-covered map removes that information and changes overlap cells from blue to cyan.
